sources.title: SuperPlane README
sources.locator: About section; factory board hero image; Getting started; Community and license
sources.finding: SuperPlane turns high-confidence backlog issues into verified, review-ready pull requests; coordinates coding agents, source control, CI, review, approvals and feedback on one visible board; offers SuperPlane Cloud signup plus Docker Compose and Kubernetes self-hosting; licensed Apache 2.0.

sources.title: SuperPlane Prod factory board image
sources.locator: Full board: Backlog, Implement, Verify, Done columns with task cards, confidence bars, Review/Mergeable/Merged/Closed badges, filters All/My/Unassigned

sources.title: SuperPlane pricing
sources.locator: Plans 01-04; Usage Costs; Compare Plans table; FAQ
sources.finding: Plans: Pay-as-you-go $0/mo + usage (10 seats, 5 parallel tasks); Starter $20/org/mo + usage (10 seats, unlimited parallel); Team $50/user/mo + usage (up to 50 seats, BYOK); Enterprise custom (SSO, audit logs, configurable retention, priority support, enterprise self-hosting). Credits for sandbox/model use with scheduled auto-purchase; provider rates +10% for SuperPlane tokens; Codex subscription and API keys carry no token markup; sandbox time separate; card required for pay-as-you-go.

sources.title: SuperPlane Privacy Policy
sources.locator: Sections 1-3: information collected and sharing
sources.finding: Collects account, billing (via third-party processor), communications, usage (workflows, machine/model use, error logs), device/log data, PostHog/Google Analytics website data, and third-party integration data including source code, pull requests, issue descriptions and comments; shares with service providers; no sale of personal information stated.

sources.title: SuperPlane Security Policy
sources.locator: Sections 1-9: data, execution, approvals, retention, compliance
sources.finding: Source cloned into ephemeral isolated environments and not permanently stored; runner components run in dedicated isolated ephemeral VMs/containers destroyed after execution; secrets AES-256 encrypted, decrypted in memory only; human approvals plus RBAC; logs retained limited period then auto-deleted, account deletion destroys data; US hosting; ZDR via OpenRouter for managed models; GitHub/GitLab granular scopes revocable anytime; SOC 2 compliance actively being worked towards, not yet attained.

sources.title: SuperPlane API reference
sources.locator: Developer reference: OpenAPI 3 spec, schema source v1.0.0-rc7
sources.finding: Publishes an OpenAPI 3 specification generated from application protobuf definitions for v1.0.0-rc7; spec download needs no auth but API requests require workspace credentials and permissions; self-hosted installations use their own base URL.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: pipeline overview
sources.locator: Pipeline at a glance: Backlog, Implement, Verify, Done stage table
sources.finding: Pipeline stages: Backlog (approved task with context), Implement (branch/PR with explanation), Verify (evidence or feedback), Done (completed task with preserved result/history); people and agents share the same view of work, evidence and decisions.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: quickstart
sources.locator: Prerequisites; 4 setup steps; Tips for your first run
sources.finding: First run in under 5 minutes: create account, connect a GitHub repo through intake (recent issues auto-import), open the board across Backlog/Implement/Verify/Done; start with a small bug, test fix, doc update or dependency update; use defaults before changing agents, automations or verification.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: how SuperPlane works
sources.locator: Steps 1-6: import, assess, track, configure, verify, human control
sources.finding: Connects tickets, coding agents, source control, CI and review; intake automations import matching tickets and record confidence; lines give agents a controlled path; verification and failure handling precede review; people keep decision control.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: work intake and backlog
sources.locator: Where tasks come from; readiness; confidence routing; Start authorization
sources.finding: Factories receive work from connected trackers or board-created tasks with source attached; ready tasks state problem, expected behavior, scope, evidence and constraints; confidence score routes (ready vs needs clarification); the Start action is the authorization boundary and implementation begins only after team rules are met.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: intakes overview
sources.locator: Choose a source; define imports; assess; try one task
sources.finding: Intake sources: GitHub issues/events, Jira, Linear, Sentry events; filter by repo/project/label/state; each task needs requested change, repo/area, source link and a confirming test or check; backlog automation assesses confidence before implementation starts.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: backlog automation
sources.locator: Decide entries; analysis context; route results; start decision; cost control
sources.finding: Backlog automation imports/enriches/scores work; routes passed/failed/human-review outcomes; keeps the Start decision visible (automated start only via narrow trusted-repo/label/threshold rules); cost controls include filtering before agent nodes, smaller classification models and no re-analysis until task/context changes.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: Implement
sources.locator: Workflow vs agent jobs; typical run; durable execution
sources.finding: Implement converts approved tasks to concrete changes; the factory owns sequence and guardrails while the coding agent inspects the repo, edits, runs checks and prepares review; durable execution records state between steps so runs resume from a known boundary instead of restarting; transient errors retry, failing tests return to the agent with output, product decisions pause for a person.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: Implement automation
sources.locator: Shape the agent; explicit repo actions; failure path; model spend
sources.finding: Implement automation sets target repo/branch, task plus analysis, AGENTS.md-style instructions, build/test/lint commands, off-limit paths and required outputs (commit, branch, PR summary); source-control nodes attach branch/PR artifacts and update existing PRs rather than duplicating; agent failure output is recorded with logs; model/stage sizing and deterministic bookkeeping nodes control spend.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: Verify
sources.locator: Evidence stack; failed-check feedback; run vs result quality; human attention
sources.finding: Verify combines repository checks, PR state, task-specific checks, agent review and human review; failed deterministic checks return command plus failure output to implementation in a bounded correction loop; execution failure and verification failure are distinguished; human attention covers tradeoffs, sensitive dependencies, ambiguous requirements and scope calls.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: Verify automation
sources.locator: Check/process configuration; review feedback without losing context
sources.finding: Verify automation runs required checks and review feedback against the implementation output, preserving task context across correction attempts and recording which checks passed or failed for the task.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: Done
sources.locator: Completion rules; preserved record; handoff to people; operating data
sources.finding: Done means the factory completion rule is met (e.g. PR ready after required checks, optionally approved/merged), not that an agent stopped; the record preserves source issue, branch/commit/PR, agent output, checks, approvals, retries/failures and timestamps; factories may leave merge to repo owners or include approval and merge; timing/stage/retry/intervention signals feed task-selection improvements.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: automations
sources.locator: Policy outside prompts; edit canvas or via agent; cost controls; per-stage customization
sources.finding: Automations define per-stage triggers, agents, integrations, checks, failure routes and human decisions; editable via canvas or by describing the outcome to an agent (staged graph reviewed before save); deterministic nodes handle filters/status/routing/notifications; per-stage model choice; concurrency limits where tasks share a repo; focused failure context; repeated attempts stop when access, clarification or approval is needed.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: factory costs
sources.locator: Cost categories; per-task trend; trace causes; reduce spend
sources.finding: Cost reporting shows token spend (recorded input/output for supported managed models) and compute spend (supported managed machine time) attributed to closed tasks, with a per-task median-spend-by-day trend; traces increases to repeated attempts, oversized models, unrelated context, long pre-failure sessions, verification loops and unaccepted closes; external provider charges are not automatically represented.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: billing overview
sources.locator: Choose a plan; Compare plan features; Understand usage charges (sandbox time, model use, funding); Self-hosting
sources.finding: Billing overview now mirrors the pricing page: pay-as-you-go $0 plus usage (10 seats, 5 parallel tasks, card required), Starter $20 per organization plus usage (10 seats, unlimited parallel tasks), Team $50 per user plus usage (up to 50 seats, provider API keys, budget limits, priority support), Enterprise custom (SSO, audit logs, enterprise self-hosting and onboarding). Credits fund sandbox time, charged separately under every model source, and SuperPlane-provided tokens at provider rate plus 10% on pay-as-you-go, Starter and Team (Enterprise custom); own keys and ChatGPT subscriptions carry no token markup. Top up or schedule automatic purchases; budget controls live on Team and Enterprise.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: bring your own key
sources.locator: Connect the key; model choice; run and billing effects
sources.finding: Maintainer/Admin connects a Claude, OpenAI or OpenRouter API key as the workspace model source; agents run on that key with provider-side billing and no 10% platform fee while machine time stays on SuperPlane usage; OpenAI API keys are separate from ChatGPT subscriptions.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: bring your own subscription
sources.locator: Connect ChatGPT; workspace source; assign work; what you pay
sources.finding: Each member connects a personal ChatGPT subscription; the workspace selects ChatGPT subscriptions as its model source with a default task owner; each task runs Codex on its owner's subscription and allowed models; the plan covers model use while SuperPlane bills machine time; switching replaces the default owner on every intake including scheduled ones; Maintainer/Admin required.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: model sources
sources.locator: Compare the sources: SuperPlane, API key, ChatGPT subscriptions
sources.finding: Each workspace runs agents on exactly one model source: SuperPlane-managed (provider rate +10%), own API key (Claude/OpenAI/OpenRouter, provider-billed), or ChatGPT subscriptions (owner plan covers Codex); the choice applies to every automation and switching replaces the agent; machine time is billed in all three routes.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: connect an MCP client
sources.locator: Endpoint; Cursor/Claude Code configuration; OAuth authorization; revocation
sources.finding: Workspace MCP server at https://app.superplane.com/mcp (remote Streamable HTTP) with OAuth sign-in, organization/workspace-scoped approval and per-connection revocation; documented Cursor mcp.json and Claude Code CLI registration; self-hosted installations use their own origin plus /mcp.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: install and connect the CLI
sources.locator: Install; API token auth; inspect workspaces/tasks; self-hosted connection
sources.finding: Product CLI via npm @superplane/cli (macOS/Linux x64/arm64; Windows not supported by npm distribution) or install script; API-token auth via SUPERPLANE_URL/SUPERPLANE_TOKEN with saved context; inspects workspaces and tasks (workspace active/list, tasks list, JSON output); connects to self-hosted origins without /api/v1 suffix.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: agent tools
sources.locator: Tasks, people/ownership, checks, artifacts tool reference; runner credentials
sources.finding: Agents manage factory work through MCP or the runner Bash superplane task CLI: list/create/close tasks with keys and states, list members with roles and open counts, assign owners (with only-if-unassigned), record/remove scored checks, attach/read/remove artifacts; SuperPlane injects per-run credentials and PATH; task queries use the current workspace; both interfaces share the same permissions.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: source control and work intake
sources.locator: GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket; Jira/Linear/ServiceNow; access guidance
sources.finding: GitHub manages issues, branches, PRs, comments, checks and repo events; GitLab/Bitbucket react to repo events and manage resources; Jira/Linear manage issues, ServiceNow service records; guidance requires dedicated minimum-scope connections able to read the backlog and create branches/PRs.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: CI/CD
sources.locator: Supported tools; trigger-wait-route pattern; production approvals
sources.finding: CircleCI, Harness, Octopus Deploy, Render, Semaphore, Cloudsmith and JFrog Artifactory integrations trigger pipelines after branch/PR readiness, wait for results, attach checks and route failures back; production deployments stay behind required approval and policy checks.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: cloud and infrastructure
sources.locator: Cloud providers; platforms and registries
sources.finding: AWS, Google Cloud, Azure, OCI, DigitalOcean, Hetzner and Cloudflare components plus DockerHub, Coolify, Render, Cloudsmith and JFrog Artifactory for build/delivery; narrow credentials with recorded approvals before destructive or production actions.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: observability
sources.locator: Telemetry/alerts; incident workflows
sources.finding: Datadog, Dash0, Grafana, Honeycomb, Logfire, New Relic, Prometheus and Sentry supply investigation evidence; PagerDuty, FireHydrant, incident.io and Rootly drive incident workflows; read-only investigation first, approval required before changing production.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: custom integrations
sources.locator: HTTP/GraphQL; webhook trigger; SSH; safe design
sources.finding: Core components cover REST (HTTP Request), GraphQL, inbound webhook triggers (external URL starts an automation, with authentication and payload validation), and SSH commands with organization secrets; safe design requires minimum permissions, timeouts, failure paths, credential-free logs and human approval before high-impact changes.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: all components
sources.locator: Coding agents and AI; core workflow; source control; delivery controls
sources.finding: Component catalog: core triggers/approvals/control-flow/HTTP/GraphQL/SSH/memory/factory actions; Daytona sandboxes; coding agents and AI via workspace model source (Claude, Cursor, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Perplexity listed); source control, CI/CD, cloud, observability, communication (Discord, Teams, SendGrid, Slack, SMTP, Telegram) and delivery controls (LaunchDarkly).

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: self-host overview
sources.locator: Single VM; cloud install; Fleet Manager runner VMs
sources.finding: Single-VM Docker Compose install on Linux or Enterprise Kubernetes (Terraform/Helm) on AWS/Azure/GCP; owner setup installs Fleet Manager which starts runner VMs from runner images; self-hosted users cover their own infrastructure and model costs; Kubernetes installs require an Enterprise license.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: install on your cloud
sources.locator: Terraform flow; owner account; Fleet Manager run commands
sources.finding: Enterprise cloud install runs Terraform (cluster, Postgres, storage, Helm release), kubectl/Helm setup, DNS, browser owner setup and product-printed Fleet Manager commands; runner images per architecture; Fleet Manager installs Runner v0.2.1.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: why open source
sources.locator: What is Open: Apache 2.0; public development; flexible operation
sources.finding: The public repository holds the engine, web interface, API definitions, integrations, dev environment and tests under Apache 2.0 with public development; run in cloud or on own infrastructure with chosen models; open-source project plus managed cloud offering.

sources.title: SuperPlane docs: latest release notes

sources.title: SuperPlane Core components doc
sources.locator: Schedule trigger; Webhook trigger; Approval component
sources.finding: Schedule trigger starts executions on minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/cron (5- or 6-field) schedules with timezones; Webhook trigger starts a chain when called; Approval pauses execution and waits for required approvers (users, groups or roles) with approved/rejected channels.

sources.title: SuperPlane scheduled intake doc
sources.locator: Setup form; backend template; prompt contract
sources.finding: Scheduled intake adds a Backlog-column entry with a daily time or cron expression (browser-timezone offset stored); backend instantiates a bundled template resolving repo, branch, Git integration and hosted/BYOK agent; the agent writes /tmp/proposal.json and only a valid non-empty proposal creates a task; creation does not start a manual run.

sources.title: SuperPlane Daytona component doc
sources.locator: Create Repository Sandbox; Create/Delete Sandbox; Execute Code/Command; Preview URL
sources.finding: Daytona components create isolated sandboxes, clone a repository, run bootstrap scripts, execute code/commands and delete the environment; clone plus bootstrap run sequentially with error returns.

sources.title: SuperPlane Claude component doc
sources.locator: Run Managed Agent; Run Code Agent; Text Prompt; Files API
sources.finding: Claude components run a managed agent in Anthropic's managed environment, run an autonomous coding agent against a repository that opens/updates a PR, send Messages API prompts, batch requests and fetch Claude Code usage metrics; Files API enabled per request with sessions scoped to the API key workspace.

sources.title: SuperPlane Cursor component doc
sources.locator: Launch Cloud Agent; Get Daily Usage Data
sources.finding: Cursor components launch cloud agents for asynchronous coding tasks and fetch team usage metrics (lines added/accepted, requests, subscription vs usage-based counts) via Cursor Admin API keys.

sources.finding: Approval nodes implement pending/approved/rejected states with per-record approve/reject operations gated by configured approvers; combined with the documented Approval trigger this enforces human gates (e.g. before merge or production deploy) inside the workflow.

sources.title: Run cancellation actions

sources.finding: Server exposes cancel-execution and cancel-run operations with a run-cancellation notifier; release notes confirm active runs can be cancelled asynchronously, so stop terminates execution while the task and its history remain.

sources.finding: Factory line steps cap in-flight runs via MaxParallelism with a default of 10; dispatch acquires parallelism slots and waiters move in as slots release, providing the queueing behind the documented concurrency controls.

sources.locator: sendPlanningSessionMessage lines 101-159; loadPlanningSession lines 334-355
sources.finding: An authorized workspace user loads a planning session by organization, factory and session ID, then SendUserMessage records the current user ID in that same session. The handler does not restrict messages to a creator; participating senders are added as draft assignees. The shared planning agent can therefore receive instructions from multiple humans.

sources.title: SuperPlane self-hosted analytics configuration
sources.locator: docs/product-analytics.md lines 1-10; web_src/src/posthog.ts initPostHog; pkg/productanalytics/analytics.go New
sources.finding: The product analytics guide states events are sent only when POSTHOG_KEY is set. The server creates a no-op client for an empty key and the browser does not initialize PostHog without its injected key. Self-hosted operators can leave POSTHOG_KEY unset to disable product analytics; this does not establish a hosted-user opt-out or disable operational tracing.

sources.finding: The injected runner tool list supports task list/create/close, current-task owner assignment, checks and artifacts, but no agent-session delegation/start/inspection or messaging tool. Agents cannot move tasks between columns; deterministic product canvases sequence the stage agents. A general automation canvas is not an agent coordinator role.
